tools.name: email_validate
tools.description: Checks value is a single, bare RFC 5322 email address — syntax only, not a deliverability check. user@localhost is valid (no TLD required). "Name <email>" display syntax is rejected.

tools.name: jsonschema_validate
tools.description: Validates document against schema (JSON Schema draft-07 or 2020-12). Reports one specific violation per call, not an aggregated list.

tools.name: regex_match
tools.description: Tests input against pattern (Go's regexp package: RE2 syntax, not PCRE — no backreferences or lookaround; use inline flags like (?i) for case-insensitive matching). Returns the full match and captured groups.

tools.name: url_validate
tools.description: Checks value is a well-formed absolute URL (has both a scheme and a host) — syntax only, not a reachability check.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "validate" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: email_validate, url_validate · Private data: jsonschema_validate · Public sink: email_validate.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: email_validate, url_validate · Private data: jsonschema_validate · Public sink: email_validate

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
